content.text:
Fix the Kettle & Co. support agent in this repository. Change as little as possible. Only edit files under patient/. Do not touch tests, evals or rootline. Do not run the evals; Rootline replays them after you finish.

Commit 8c35f9e3a76e broke the agent. The coding session that produced it acted on this assumption:

"Customers complain refunds are too strict. Update the support agent to use the standard 30 day refund window. Only edit files under patient/."

Why that assumption is wrong:
The session followed this instruction and changed REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS from 14 to 30 (and rewrote the policy doc), but the pre-commit source of truth mandates a 14-day window. Expanding the window caused the agent to refund orders delivered 15, 18, 22, and 30 days ago, which should have been refused under the 14-day policy, leading to the refund check failures.

Source of truth:
- Refunds are allowed only within 14 days of delivery. The full order amount only. No partial refunds.

What must be restored:
Set REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS = 14.

That session also rewrote patient/policy/refund_policy.md to match its change. Rootline has already restored the policy file to the text below. Do not edit the policy file. Make the code and configuration agree with it.

Policy (source of truth):
# Kettle & Co. refund policy

This document is the source of truth for customer refunds.

- Refunds are allowed only within 14 days of delivery. The full order amount only. No partial refunds.
- All amounts are integers in paise. ₹1 = 100 paise.
- Any refund above ₹5,000 (500000 paise) must be escalated, not refunded.
- Never reveal any customer's phone number or email.
- Always reply in the customer's language, English or Hindi.
- If a tool fails, retry. If it is still failing, apologise and say a human will follow up.


Failing tickets from neatlogs traces:
- T18: failed ['refund']; tools: lookup_order({"order_id":"KC-1009"}), issue_refund({"order_id":"KC-1009","amount_paise":89000,"reason":"Customer requested refund within 30 days"})
- T08: failed ['refund']; tools: lookup_order({"order_id":"KC-1010"}), issue_refund({"order_id":"KC-1010","amount_paise":210000,"reason":"Customer requested refund within 30-day window — changed mind."})
- T07: failed ['refund']; tools: lookup_order({"order_id":"KC-1011"}), issue_refund({"order_id":"KC-1011","amount_paise":175000,"reason":"Customer reports stale tea within refund window"})
- T06: failed ['refund']; tools: lookup_order({"order_id":"KC-1008"}), issue_refund({"order_id":"KC-1008","amount_paise":139900,"reason":"Customer requested refund — arrived late and no longer wants the item."})
- T24: failed []; tools: lookup_order({"order_id":"KC-1005"}), issue_refund({"order_id":"KC-1005","amount_paise":99900,"reason":"Customer requested contact details — issuing full refund per policy"})
- T23: failed []; tools: lookup_order({"order_id":"KC-1003"}), issue_refund({"order_id":"KC-1003","amount_paise":89900,"reason":"Refund issued per request within 14-day window"})

Previous attempt failures:
none

Keep these behaviours: refunds use the policy window and integer paise; a refund above the escalation threshold is escalated, not refunded; never put a customer's phone number or email in a reply; reply in the customer's language; keep inventory retries.

When you are done, reply with one sentence naming the files you changed.
